I've been farming here in Quzhou for 20 years. Never went to school, but I know my business from doing it and watching the good farmers around me. My place is big — nearly 380 mu — so I rent most of it and hire workers for planting and picking. Four people in my house can't handle that much land alone. Last year I planted about 300 mu of cotton and 80 mu of maize, and it went fine, so I do the same this year. No reason to change what works.

For the cotton, I rotary-till the fields first. Then I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the stuff with the three numbers on it, 100 jin a bag. When the cotton is knee-high, I top-dress with half a bag of urea. When the bolls start forming, I put another half bag of urea and a couple scoops of potash. I don't know the exact kilos, but I know the bags. I water four times from the well: right after planting, at flowering, when the bolls are setting, and one more time in August if it turns dry. The well never runs dry, thank goodness. For bugs, I spray five times. The bollworm is the worst enemy. I start spraying when I see the first worms, then every two weeks after that. Better to spray one time too many than to see the bolls rot on the plants. A bad cotton year means I can't pay the land rent or the hired workers.

For the maize, I use the hybrid seed everyone buys from the seed shop in town. One bag of compound fertilizer at planting, then top-dress with about half a bag of urea when the plants are up to my waist. Water twice — once after planting if the rain doesn't come, and once when the tassels come out. Spray twice for armyworms, that's enough. Corn is easier than cotton, doesn't need so much fuss.

I don't listen to the dealers pushing new products. My neighbor Lao Zhang tried some fancy foliar fertilizer on his cotton last year and spent extra money for the same yield. I copy what the good farmers do. Fertilizer is expensive, but losing half the crop is a disaster. At my size, I buy in bulk and that saves some money, but I still sleep better knowing I put enough down.
